senses.d: The result or outcome of a cause.
ex: The effect of the hurricane was a devastated landscape.

senses.d: Impression left on the mind; sensation produced.
ex: patchwork […] introduced for oratorical effect
The effect was heightened by the wild and lonely nature of the place.

senses.d: Execution; performance; realization; operation.
ex: That no compunctious visitings of nature / Shake my fell purpose, nor keep peace between / The effect and it.

senses.d: The state of being binding and enforceable, as in a rule, policy, or law.
ex: The new law will come into effect on the first day of next year.

senses.d: An illusion produced by technical means (as in "special effect")
ex: The effect of flying was most convincing.

senses.d: An alteration, or device for producing an alteration, in sound after it has been produced by an instrument.
ex: I use an echo effect here to make the sound more mysterious.
I just bought a couple of great effects.

senses.d: A scientific phenomenon, usually named after its discoverer.
ex: Doppler effect

senses.d: An influence or causal association between two variables.
ex: effect size
therapeutic effect

senses.d: Belongings, usually as personal effects.
ex: His Goods, Family, and all his Effects were also ſeiz'd every where, and his Family carried into Priſon.

senses.d: Consequence intended; purpose; meaning; general intent; with to.
ex: They spake to her to that effect.

senses.d: To make or bring about; to implement.
ex: The best way to effect change is to work with existing stakeholders.

ety.text: 1398, “making,” from Old French, from Latin efficientem, nominative efficiēns, participle of efficere (“work out, accomplish”) (see effect). Meaning “productive, skilled” is from 1787. Efficiency apartment is first recorded 1930, American English.

senses.d: Making good, thorough, or careful use of resources; not consuming extra. Especially, making good use of time or energy.
ex: An efficient process would automate all the routine work.
Our cleaners are almost too efficient: they throw away anything left out on a desk.

senses.d: Expressing the proportion of consumed energy that was successfully used in a process; the ratio of useful output to total input.
ex: The motor is only 20% efficient at that temperature.

senses.d: Causing effects, producing results; bringing into being; initiating change (rare except in philosophical and legal expression efficient cause = causative factor or agent).
ex: Ownership, maintenance, or use of the automobile need not be the direct and efficient cause of the injury sustained
It was well said of Plotinus, that the stars were significant, but not efficient.

senses.d: effective, efficacious

senses.d: A cause; something that causes an effect.
